question.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{3}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{csc}⁡({x}^{3})\operatorname{cot}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{csc}⁡({x}^{3})\operatorname{cot}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{csc}⁡u\operatorname{cot}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡u+C \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡({x}^{3})+C\end{aligned}
$$
